subject: clipping issue with AX6 Axivity data

messages.author: 38bcfc422ee452f7
messages.subject: clipping issue with AX6 Axivity data
parts:
Hello,

I’m using GGIR (v 2.7-1) to analyse AX6 Axivity data.  We have 600+ *.cwa data files, which have 7 days of data, including gyroscope data.

The GGIR function runs successfully with no errors, but I have very large clipping scores in the part2summary – the average is 0.65, with 99% of values greater than 0.01. According to the vignette the clipping score 'should be 0'.

The data are from 100 accelerometers, so it’s unlikely that they’re all faulty, and the dynamic range is set to the default 8g. Looking at a few of the datasets in OmGUI doesn’t show any obvious issues with the data.

I'm running this on a Linux high performance cluster, but get the same problem on Windows 10 with default parameters: GGIR(datadir=acceldir, outputdir=outputdir)

 I have a suspicion it's to do with the gyroscope data - has anyone else had problems with AX6 data when collecting gyroscope data, or found a solution?

Thanks,

Ruth

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] clipping issue with AX6 Axivity data
parts:
Hello Ruth,

Can you please try the GGIR development version, see installation instruction here:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#2_Setting_up_your_work_environment

Please let me know if this addresses the issue.

Further, it might be that the dynamic range of the sensor is currently assumed to be 8 g for AX6, which would have to be updated to match the dynamic range as extracted from the file header. However, I suspect that that is not the issue here.

Thanks,

Vincent
